name: Shakuni
role: Prince of Gandhara, maternal uncle of the Kauravas and master of dice
summary: In the Mahabharata, Shakuni is the brother of Gandhari and uncle of Duryodhana, remembered for the dice game that cost the Pandavas their kingdom, and also honoured in a Kerala shrine.
about: In the Mahabharata, Shakuni is a prince of Gandhara and the brother of Gandhari, who marries the blind king Dhritarashtra. He lives at Hastinapura with his sister's sons and becomes a close adviser to Duryodhana. After the Pandavas' great Rajasuya ceremony, Duryodhana is jealous, and Shakuni offers a plan to win Yudhishthira's wealth at dice. The epic describes the game that follows, the loss of the kingdom and the thirteen years of exile, as turning points of the whole story. In the war he fights with the Kauravas and, according to the epic, is killed by Sahadeva on the eighteenth day. The name Shakuni points to a large bird and sometimes to a vulture. Retellings differ on his motives: Jain retellings and the Odia Mahabharata give different reasons for his anger. In Kerala, a temple in Kollam is dedicated to him.
kidSummary: Shakuni is Duryodhana's uncle in the Mahabharata. He is famous for the dice game that began the long exile of the Pandavas. In Kerala, there is a temple where people honour him, which shows that the same story can be read in different ways.

story.title: A prince from Gandhara
story.text: In the Mahabharata, Shakuni is a prince of the mountain kingdom Gandhara. When his sister Gandhari marries the blind Dhritarashtra, he comes with her to live at Hastinapura.

story.title: Jealousy after the feast
story.text: After the Pandavas hold their grand Rajasuya, Duryodhana stays on to look at their wealth and grows jealous. Shakuni offers to help win it all in a game of dice.

story.title: The dice game
story.text: Yudhishthira accepts the game, but Shakuni plays for Duryodhana. The Pandavas lose their kingdom, and finally a stake is set that sends them into thirteen years of exile.

story.title: The war
story.text: In the great war at Kurukshetra, Shakuni fights on the Kaurava side. The epic says Sahadeva, the youngest Pandava, ends his life on the eighteenth day.

story.title: A shrine in Kerala
story.text: In Pavithreswaram near Kottarakkara in Kerala, a village temple honours Shakuni. Local tradition says he found peace there after the war.

teaches: Jealousy can grow into great harm
Fair play matters in any game
Stories can be read in more than one way
emblems: Granite throne at the Kerala temple

facts.text: Shakuni means a large bird, often a vulture. He is also called Kitava, the gambler, and Parvatiya, the man from the mountains, and the epic names him grandmaster of dicing.
The Adi Parva compares Duryodhana to a tree of wrath and calls Shakuni one of its branches.
Playing as Duryodhana's stand-in, Shakuni threw the dice twenty times against Yudhishthira, and Yudhishthira lost every throw, giving up his wealth, servants, brothers and finally himself.

The epic calls Shakuni an incarnation of Dvapara, the presiding spirit of the third age. After the war, Vyasa called up the souls of the fallen, Shakuni's among them, and a later book says his soul rejoined Dvapara.
Even Shakuni once advised Duryodhana to give the Pandavas their kingdom back (Vana Parva, chapter 251), but the advice was ignored.

After the dice game, the youngest Pandava, Sahadeva, vowed to be the one to defeat Shakuni. On day eighteen Shakuni struck Sahadeva's head with a lance, but Sahadeva recovered, killed Shakuni's son Uluka, and then ended Shakuni with an arrow.

Jain retellings marry Gandhari to a goat first, and Bhishma then punishes her family. Another telling, in the Odia Mahabharata, jails them for refusing the marriage, with Duryodhana sometimes playing the jailer in place of Bhishma.

Some versions say Shakuni made his dice from the bones of his relatives, with his father's spirit guiding them. The Sanskrit epic tells it differently: his brothers attended the Rajasuya and fought in the war.
Scholars note how much maternal relatives matter in the Mahabharata: Shakuni stays close to his sister Gandhari and her sons, while Krishna, the Pandavas' maternal cousin, helps them throughout.
When Bhishma went to Gandhara to arrange Gandhari's marriage, her father Subala hesitated because Dhritarashtra was blind, then agreed after weighing the Kuru family's good name.
Before the game, Shakuni told Dhritarashtra he had noticed that Yudhishthira played dice poorly despite loving the game, and planned to use that weakness.
Duryodhana said he could not go on if the plan was refused, and Dhritarashtra, shaken by his son's distress, gave in despite Vidura's repeated pleas.
During the game Dhritarashtra, caught up in the excitement, kept eagerly asking after each throw whether Shakuni had won.
In battle, a warrior named Iravan killed five of Shakuni's brothers, and later Bhima's onslaught killed five more.
Shakuni tried illusion tricks against Arjuna, but Arjuna countered them and Shakuni had to leave the field.
A village temple at Pavithreswaram near Kottarakkara in Kerala is dedicated to Shakuni and run by the Kurava community; a granite throne there is said to have been his.
At the Kerala shrine there is no ordinary building or priestly puja. Local offerings include tender coconut and silk.
Shakuni's home kingdom, Gandhara, lay in what is today Pakistan.
The game is called Pasha in the epic, a dice game linked to the family of games that includes Pachisi.
The Pavithreswaram shrine's festival, called Malakkuda Mahotsavam, is held in the Malayalam month of Makaram. Nearby are subsidiary deities including Bhuvaneswari Devi, Kiratha Moorthi and Nagaraja.
In Kollam district, a temple at Poruvazhy honours Duryodhana. It has no idol, and devotees make their offering through a ritual called Sankalpam.

quiz.q: What does the word shakuni mean in Sanskrit?
quiz.why: Shakuni means a large bird, often a vulture.

quiz.q: Who was Shakuni's sister, who covered her eyes after marriage?
quiz.why: Gandhari wrapped a cloth over her eyes out of devotion to her blind husband.

quiz.q: Which Pandava is said to have ended Shakuni's life in the war?
quiz.why: In the epic, Sahadeva, the youngest Pandava, is the one who defeats Shakuni.

quiz.q: In which Indian state is there a village temple dedicated to Shakuni?
quiz.why: Pavithreswaram near Kottarakkara in Kerala has a temple that honours him.
